blockers.title: Sleep harms the rule-from-examples skills

The pooled-5 guard was blind to it, so the earlier 'no harm' claim on the 71.3% fast-sleep win is withdrawn (harm unmeasured). Suspected cause: the night learning rate (1e-3) with a fresh optimiser. Test R (self-repair practice) made it worse and is dropped. UPDATE 10:30 AM ET: cause found. It is overfitting from re-reading a small reused row set (32 visits per record), not the learning rate. Fresh rows improve skills (+1.6 to +2.3). UPDATE 11:33 AM ET: screen L (lr 1e-4) removes the loss on both parents and keeps nearly all of the C2 gain (one parent 0.3 under its bar).

blockers.title: Skills pretraining stalls near 72/100 (pass mark 80)
blockers.detail: PC runs: skmain2 72, skmain3 65, main4 71, all below 80 (checkpoints kept). Diagnosis at 4:20 PM ET: the model cannot memorize 2,000 practised questions (48% against an 85% mark), and more practice adds only +10. Multi-step skills are at 15%. Combined with fair scaling, the block is outside the core. Suspected cause was the 32-wide pipes and the 8-slot averaged output, but screen v1 found wider pipes, 8 loops, lower learning rate and the pointer exit each had no effect on fit (all about 48-50%). Stiffness, core size and cut-off inputs are ruled out. Screen v2 (exit width 32 to 256) added only +0.7 fit over 3 seeds. Five changes have failed; suspect the frozen 1.2B is the cap. Blocker-paper ideas (Opus, from 20 papers): the likely cause is that the core's 8 hint vectors sit before the question, and prefix hints cannot redirect attention (Petrov et al. 2023), so they only elicit skills the 1.2B already has. Eval bug found at 10:15 PM ET: question words were fed twice at answer time vs once in training, so all skills scores ran about 6 points low. Corrected, main2 scores 74.6% on practised skills, not 68.5%, so the real plateau is higher than 72. Screen v3: a rank-8 LoRA hurt fit (50% to 12%) at the learning rate used. Update 10:33 PM ET: eval bug fixed in PR #38; corrected fit on practised skills is 67% (was reading 49%), mark 85, gap 18 points. Earlier fit numbers (48-50%) were read with the bug, so the 'cannot memorize' diagnosis is weaker than first thought. Update 10:58 PM ET: a talker that writes worked steps before the answer lifted practised skills 67 to 78% and new kinds 48 to 70% (3 runs); chain puzzles 86-99%. Still under the 85 mark. Update 12:26 AM ET: a 3.2M char-level transformer from scratch scores 75.7% in-distribution (4 seeds) vs 74.6% for the 1.2B sandwich, so the 1.2B adds little on practised skills; both are ~0% on 4 unpractised skills. Update 3:32 AM ET: SR2 worked steps reach the 85% mark on 3 seeds, but swap tests show the talker does that thinking and the core can't learn to add. Partial fix: the core plans the sums (which numbers, which operations) and an exact calculator runs the plan; this scores 87% on new chain questions without the talker, matching the talker's own steps. Pending 5 confirmation seeds. Update 5:02 AM ET: plan-plus-calculator scores 97.6% on new chain questions across 6 seeds (minimum 95.6%), beating the talker's own steps at 87%. The fix was decaying the learning rate to zero. Caveat: the thinker had more practice questions, so a matched test is needed. Update 5:50 AM ET: the 97.6% plan-plus-calculator result depended on extra practice (17k questions). Matched practice: thinker's plan 82.8% vs talker's steps 85.8% over 6 paired seeds, about level, still under the 85 mark for the plan. Update 7:24 AM ET: with matched practice (17k questions + lr decay) the LM writing its own steps scores 98.8% on new chain questions (2 runs), level with the plan route's 97.6%, so the thinker does not beat the talker. What holds: in the real model with the plan route, swapping plans drops chain answers from about 157/160 to 2 (the thinker decides them), and the model gets 89.6% of all new questions (3 runs). Update 6:33 PM ET: two-hop pointer (76/160) and 2048 thinker reader (77/160) are both flat against 77, so pointer and door designs are ruled out as the limit on the 4 lookup kinds.
blockers.next: Ultracode thread: keep checking the plan route on more skill families and the 89.6% overall figure against the 85 mark; custom reader/talker designs are also being judged.

misses: Creative job 7 'keep the parts' DONE (12:55 AM ET): between the marks on both parents. Multi-step gain +0.6 and +3.2 (need +10), no climb. Skills kept (add/multiply up to 95-96%). Cause: the search finds too few multi-step answers to learn from.
EGK (the fix for one EGE mark) crashed with NaN on seed 201.
Memory sleep 6-seed confirm failed one mark: skill harm of -3.9 on s205, caused by the 'answer note' (harm 0 on all 6 with it off).

Plan B Test B1 proved wrong (+0.78 vs +15 needed; students about 11% on new kinds, memorised practice 91-96%). Ben chose 'Wait for web text' (9:32 AM ET): no 100M student; Plan B continues via roadmap 8a 10M web-text rung.
EGT (Gemma as a training-only teacher, shipping at 3.3M) FAILS: pooled-5 +0.18 and +0.61 (needs +1) and variant +2.54 (needs +3).

Fast sleep (DEV, 10:29 AM ET): answer note off gives +0.98 vs +1.0 needed; chaining nights into the notebook proved wrong (+0.7 vs +5). Fine-tuning on search records beat plain sleep by 4-8 points on 2 parents but falls between marks, not adopted.

wins.d: Memory sleep (screen, 2 seeds, not yet confirmed): learns from the night's finds by writing them into a notebook the model reads, with no weight changes. It matched the fine-tune sleep's gain (+34 and +29 vs +36 and +27) using 25 to 32 times less compute, with zero skill harm, and it kept add/multiply (32% vs 8-10%). Tuning was done on one seed, so a 6-seed confirm is next.
wins.w: Fine-tune sleep: +36 and +27, but skill harm earlier. Memory sleep: +34 and +29 at 25-32x less compute.

wins.d: C2b sleep pilot: sleeping on its own correct finds raised right first answers on new rules by +35 and +27 points on the two copies. The ideal version gained +40 and +42, so the feasibility check passed. Sleeping on wrong or relabelled tries did nothing. Caveat: almost all of the gain is the x-times-x rule; the harder rules barely moved. Scoring against the marks is pending in the build thread. Update 10:03 PM ET: the marks pass pooled, but the gain is all near-copy (square +96 and +94, last_digit +78 and +39, the hard kinds about 0). Night 2 shows no climbing. New concern: practised-kind skill dropped (0.61 to 0.11 on the stepping-stone parent; cause untested). The roadmap thread is ruling on the verdict.
wins.w: The ideal (everything-correct) version gained +40 and +42; wrong or relabelled tries gave no gain.

wins.d: C2 cleared its first gate after practice on easier versions (25% and 20% vs 14.5% needed), but mostly on one rule (x times x) and only with very random tries. Next: does sleeping on its own finds turn them into first answers, and does a second night reach the harder rules? Raw numbers: 25.4% and 19.5% vs a 10% gate, a 14.5% bar and a 4.8% chance floor; placebo 4.3% and 5.1%, plain warm-up 5.1% and 9.8%.
wins.w: Placebo and plain warm-up arms, and chance floor 4.8%. C2 stays alive.

wins.d: B2 confirm complete on all 6 seeds: B2 beats the plain transformer by +20.3 points pooled and the step-writing transformer by +6.9, ahead on 6 of 6 seeds. PASS-1 and the step-writer part of PASS-2 pass.
wins.w: Plain transformer and step-writing transformer at the same size, nothing pretrained. Still needed: pythia-31m and few-shot baselines for Ben's full criterion.

wins.d: Local teacher works: Qwen 27B on the PC runs 32 tokens/s on one stream and 112 tokens/s across 8 streams in 15 GB of video memory, with no think text in the output. Pilot N=10 finished cleanly in about 10 minutes. No spend.
wins.w: Muse Spark plan was about $8 and needed a paid key; this costs nothing.

wins.d: TEACH teacher data finished
Creative rule breaks explained and fixed (DEV only)
wins.w: B2 reuses a number its first step already used. Greying out used numbers while it samples makes every try legal and nearly triples luck: 4.7% to 13.1% on s100 and 4.6% to 13.4% on s101. DEV only, PR #45; the roadmap thread is deciding whether to adopt it.

wins.d: Creative test C1 un-blocked (gate was miscalibrated)
wins.w: The roadmap thread found the 50% rules gate was miscalibrated: a random rule-follower reaches 58%. Read correctly, the warmed model aims 3.9x to 7.9x better than chance among legal tries. This is a re-reading of the gate, not a new training result.

wins.d: Wide doors still help on the other four question kinds
wins.w: CRDW (2048 doors on the plan route) scored 291.5 vs 287.0 held-out but was ahead on only 3/6 seeds, so it does not stack by its marks. The test also widened the planner's reader by accident, making chain answers slightly worse; on the other four question kinds the doors gave +8 and were never behind.

misses: 1.2B bench final (parked): T1 lr decay to 0 HURTS (276.2 vs 287.0 held, behind on 6 of 6 seeds).
1.2B bench final: T2 quiet notes HURTS (226.5 vs 287.0 held, behind on 6 of 6 seeds).
1.2B bench final: CRDW (doors on the plan route) does not stack (291.5 vs 287.0, ahead on only 3 of 6, confounded).
Creative pilot 2 (plain sampler) fails the PC gate on both seeds: PC/N 1.15 and 1.20 against 1.6. Signal, aim and sameness pass. The used-number mask has been adopted; masked pilot 3 is next.

Creative C1 retired (1:25 PM ET), even counted per try: s101 passed at 1.66x vs the 1.6 mark, but s100 missed at 1.29x (+2.8 points; needed 1.6x and +3), and the rule needed both. T1 sealed. C2 is next.
Qwen 27B teacher dropped by Ben (3:11 PM ET) after a clean N=10 pilot: no strong-teacher run; students use the existing teach data.

C2 stopped at cold start (B2's tries on new rule kinds are at chance: 3.9% and 6.3% vs a 4.8% floor). Next: stepping stones, easier versions of the new kinds, made by code. C2 retires only if that also misses.

EGW (EmbeddingGemma into a 768-wide thinker, 22.2M trained / 293.2M whole) failed vs plain B2 on the same 5090: pooled-5 -3.39 and -5.30 on 2 seeds. It also changed the thinker width, so Gemma itself is not yet shown to hurt.
Test LR (train the answer at every loop round) failed narrowly, not adopted: +1.1 and +1.3 on the main score, but s200 dropped 0.5 at 16 rounds (limit 0.3) and scored 15.9% with zero rounds (a leak).
C2b sleep: gain is all near-copy (hard kinds about 0), night 2 shows no climbing, and practised-kind skill dropped from 0.61 to 0.11 on the stepping-stone parent (cause untested).
EmbeddingGemma arms: EGR, EGM and EGO all failed. EGE (Gemma on top of the window) beat B2 by +1.6 on s200 but fails the zero-rounds leak mark (18% vs 5% limit).

wins.d: 2048-wide doors confirmed on 6 seeds
wins.w: Held-out 274.8/320 vs 260.0 without, ahead on 5 of 6 seeds. The gain is +15, down from +26 on the first 3 seeds, so the first read was optimistic.

wins.d: Talker calls the calculator (CRT, Ben's design)
wins.w: 471/480 held chain questions over 3 seeds (direct hand-over 470) and 298/320 fit. A swapped note gives 2-14/160 and no note 31-44, so the note is used. One mark missed: on 2/3 seeds the talker copied a swapped note only 79-84% of the time (bar 90%).

wins.d: 2048-wide doors lift held-out score (3 seeds)
wins.w: Held-out 258.0 to 284.3 of 320 and practised 275.7 to 300.7, ahead on 3/3 seeds. The 6-seed confirmation is due about 8:45 PM ET.

wins.d: Custom design B2 leads the screen (but missed its mark)
wins.w: 2 seeds, nothing pretrained at 3.3M: B2 pooled 73.7% vs plain transformer with steps 67.7%, plain 54.4%, B 68.6%. Swapping another question's plan drops it to 4%, so the plan is used. Missed the pre-set mark: with the thinker off it still scores 6.76% on seed 101 against a 5% limit (word-pointer leak).

wins.d: Custom design B ties the step-writing transformer
wins.w: Screen seed 100: design B (program plus exact calculator, nothing pretrained) ties the step-writing transformer overall and gets 99.7% vs 93.5% on 5-step chains. One seed so far; seed 101 about 8:00 AM ET.

wins.d: Real model reaches 89.6% on new questions (plan route)
wins.w: With matched practice (17k questions + lr decay), the LM writing its own steps scores 98.8% on new chain questions (2 runs), level with the thinker's plan at 97.6%. In the real model, swapping plans drops chain answers from about 157/160 to 2, so the thinker decides them; overall 89.6% on new questions (3 runs) vs the 85 mark.

wins.d: Plan-plus-calculator: level with talker when practice is matched
wins.w: Earlier read of 97.6% (6 seeds, min 95.6%) used 17k extra practice questions. Matched-practice test, 6 paired seeds: thinker's plan 82.8% vs talker's steps 85.8%, about level. Downgraded from a win.

wins.d: Core plans, calculator executes (partial win, pending confirmation)
wins.w: Worked steps (SR2) reach the 85% mark on 3 seeds, but swap tests show the talker does that thinking and the core can't learn to add. Instead the core plans the sums and an exact calculator runs them: 87% on new chain questions without the talker, matching the talker's own steps. 5 more confirmation seeds running.

wins.d: Small from-scratch model matches the 1.2B sandwich
wins.w: A 3.2M char-level transformer, no pretraining, 20 min, same 200k skills rows: 75.7% in-distribution (4 seeds) vs 74.6% for the 1.2B sandwich. Sets the bar for custom reader/talker designs.

misses: Both models weak on chain families (small 2-20%, sandwich 10-32%) and about 0% on 4 unpractised skills.
Custom design A out: beats a same-size plain transformer by 10 but loses by 3 to the step-writing transformer (seed 100).
B2 failed its pre-set leak check: thinker off scores 6.76% on seed 101 vs a 5% limit.
Per-round routers (Chain-of-Experts, PLR) dropped: 131.2 vs 132.5 of 160 held, ahead on 2 of 6 seeds.
Two-hop pointer (76/160) and 2048 thinker reader (77/160) flat against 77: pointer and door designs ruled out as the limit on the 4 lookup kinds.
Swarm parked (7:09 PM ET, PR #40): training together was void because the coach stopped steering; the answer-aware picker was +2.5 on familiar questions but -0.6 on twisted ones, failing its mark.
CRT copy-fidelity mark missed: talker copied a swapped note 79-84% on 2/3 seeds vs a 90% bar.

Merged Hearer+Reader (Ben's ask) is wrong: 278.8 vs 287.0 of 320 held, ahead on 2 of 6 seeds. Chain was level; the loss was all on cipher, letter-cycle, few-shot and grouping. The Reader stays: its width was the limit, not its being separate (2048 doors gave +26).

wins.d: Worked-steps talker (Ultracode)
wins.w: Writing worked steps before the answer: practised 67 to 78%, new kinds 48 to 70% (3 runs), chain puzzles 86-99%. Still under the 85 mark.

wins.d: Eval bug fixed (PR #38)
wins.w: Question words were fed twice at answer time; fixed. Fit on practised skills reads 67% instead of 49%, so the true gap to the 85 mark is 18 points.

wins.t: Eval bug found: skills scores ran about 6 points low
wins.d: At answer time the question words were fed twice, but once in training. Corrected, main2 scores 74.6% on practised skills, not 68.5%. All skills scores so far, including the 72 plateau, were low by about 6 points. Result in RESULT-v3.md on claude/project-thread-aya9pk.

wins.t: Info-flow round 7: current talker confirmed as the best of three
wins.d: English, 6 seeds, 576 questions: current talker (16 core vectors + question words) 83%. Latency is about 3x bare to the first word and 1.3x for an 8-word answer, the same for all three variants, so the cost is the core plus the extra pass, not the re-read. Round cost about $2.30.

wins.t: 35.8M system beats the bare 1.2B (8-shot) on new kinds: 66.3% vs 62.5%
wins.d: Gain +3.8 (CI +2.9 to +4.7), mark passed, all 6 seeds. Sums are about 22% for both, and there is no calculator in this recipe.

wins.t: English reproduced on the PC: 91.9% scratch, 91.2% from main2
wins.d: Mark 80%, bare LM 75.0%, 6 seeds each. Scratch CI 90.0-93.8, main2 CI 90.0-92.5. Main2 minus scratch is -0.7, no effect. Matches the cloud result of 92.6%.
Questions per second, batch 1 / batched: 5090 19 / 358 (batch 256); 5070 Ti 18.5 / 228 (batch 128); M1 Pro 5.6 / about 21.
Opus with Sonnet helpers beat solo Opus in the judged comparison on replacing the 1.2B hearer/talker. The solo thread's top pick, the 350M LFM, is being tested and is failing early.

wins.t: Distractor fix works: 16% to 50.2% on long questions with extra numbers
wins.d: Round-7 recipe fell to 62% to 16% on the two-step chain once irrelevant numbers were added. Training with distractors: 50.2% (+33.9, up on all 6 seeds), just meeting the 50% mark. Partial: one guard missed, independent set 2 lost 3.6 vs a 3-point limit (not significant).

wins.t: English with many generated practice questions: 35% to 93%
wins.d: Same fresh questions. Bare 1.2B model with 8 examples: 75%. Gain +18 over it, all 6 seeds. Both marks set before training.
Bare 1.2B with 8 examples got 68%. +12 points, every seed above.
Gain +26.6 (interval +14.8 to +38.3), all 6 seeds up. Table layout 30% to 62%, question-first 51% to 79%. The answer still comes only from the calculator.
Skills-trained core reached 20.9% on 2 new skills after 4,000 rows; its parent reached 10.4%. Core ahead on all 6 seeds. Weight resets are not needed.

wins.t: Round 4 holds on layouts someone else wrote: 73.4%
wins.d: Mark was 70. Chat 96%, first-person 85-95%, riddle/diary 87%.
12 practised kinds scored 83% on unseen kinds; the 6-kind rerun scored 81%.

wins.t: Long questions work: 66.6% on 55-150 token questions
wins.d: Mark was 50%. Input cap lifted from 49 to 160 tokens. Short sets did not drop (-0.3, +1.4, +3.4 vs a 3-point limit).

misses: Skills fix-screen v3 (PC): the rank-8 LoRA on the 1.2B hurt fit, 50% to 12%, at the learning rate used. A gentler learning rate is untested (10:15 PM).
Skills fix-screen v2 (PC): widening the exit 32 to 256 gave +0.7 fit over 3 seeds, no effect. Five changes have now failed to move fit. Suspect: the frozen 1.2B is the cap (8:07 PM).
Skills plateau screen v1 (PR #34): wider pipes, 8 loops, lr 3e-4 and the pointer exit each had no effect on fit (all about 48-50%). About $2.80 spent, Vast boxes destroyed (6:27 PM).
Info-flow round 7 alternatives: core vectors only scored 19% even with 8000 practice questions; question-first with the second read reused scored 75% (-8 vs 83%) (5:27 PM).

Copy-talker test failed (PR #37): 13.6% on new question kinds vs 78.2% for the current talker (6 seeds), 97% on practised kinds. Swapping in another question's core state left the score at 73.2% (1 seed), so on new kinds the 1.2B answers by itself. Cheaper-talker line parked, about $0.75 (5:09 PM).
350M LM swap failed: 65.7% vs 92.6% for the 1.2B (5 of 6 seeds, each down 21-34 points), below the bare 1.2B's 75%. The model reads to a ceiling set by the LM (4:12 PM).
Fair scaling finished (6 seeds): 9.0M 64.4%, 17.9M 65.3%, 35.8M 66.3%. Scaling gain +1.9 (CI -1.0 to +4.8) vs a +5 mark, in between. Core size is not the limit (4:51 PM).
Distractor round: guard mark missed. Independent set 2 lost 3.6 points against a 3-point limit, not significant. Receipts 26%, reports 34%, first operand right only 66% (1:33 PM).
English with two kinds left out of practice: 80% vs bare 77%, too close to call. Skipping practice on a kind cost about 16 points (3:12 AM).
Extra table practice: +4.4, needed +5. No claim. That test set was partly read before the practice was written (11:15 AM).
Report/ledger practice: +3.8, needed +5. No claim. Out-of-style level is 62-76% (11:41 AM).
12 kinds vs 6 kinds of English practice: about +2, not shown. Six more new kinds tie the bare model, 78 vs 78 (12:15 PM).
Stiffness results file was lost when its box was destroyed. Scores survived in the log (12:04 PM).

wins.t: Copy path fixes unseen answers: 0-4% to 84-90%
wins.d: The model now copies the calculator result instead of looking answers up. No wrong unseen answer is a training answer.

wins.t: Varied training wording: right-call rate 81.6% to 98.1%
wins.d: Paired gain +16.5 (interval +5.6 to +27.4), all 6 seeds up. Seed spread 11.9 to 2.8 points.

wins.t: Two-step with varied wording and ordered read: 28% to 70.8%
wins.d: Gain +42.8 (interval +37 to +49). Varied wording alone 56.5% (+28.5). A second step that is a subtraction went from 0% to 66%.

misses: English first rerun passed a low bar: 4% to 35%. It memorised all 48 practice questions, and the bare 1.2B model alone gets 30% (11:47 PM).
'Think before calling': first looked like +14, six seeds said +1.9 (interval -20 to +24). Falsified; the early gain was seed luck (1:58 PM).
Sealed confirmation on new story structures: +8.5, combined 79.4% vs mark 80%. In between, not confirmed (3:47 PM).
First two-step run: only 39.9% of chains right; every second subtraction wrong (3:47 PM).
Ordered read alone: -2.4, fails (4:33 PM).
Fair scaling could not start: no working recipe yet, so it waited (9:33 AM).
Standing noise number: baseline seed spread is about 12 points, so one-seed differences under about 25 mean nothing. Marks now need 6 paired seeds.
Matching-sleep (distill) test missed: +4.5 of 200 on sums and +9.75 of 200 on grids vs a +20 bar. Doubling the true-answer loss did as well or better (4:51 PM).

coverage: Oct 3 and Oct 4 are covered from the Real model fixes, More information, Reasoner fresh-data, Fair scaling and Fernando threads plus the round write-ups. Sep 28 has one entry from the project chat; Sep 29 to Oct 2 are not summarised yet.

roadmap.n: Copy path fixed unseen answers (0-4% to 84-90%); contextual reader 72.5% to 95.5%. PR #33.
Chain 54.9% to 81.4% on our wording; 62-76% on layouts someone else wrote, so layout robustness is still a blocker.
Input cap 49 to 160 tokens, 66.6% on 55-150 token questions. With irrelevant numbers added only 50%, tracked as a blocker.
80% goal reached: 83% and 81% on never-practised kinds vs 68% for the bare 1.2B model with 8 examples. Newer kinds only tie it (78 vs 78). Reproduced on the PC: 91.9% and 91.2% vs 75.0% bare LM.

Likely near the mark: real model with plan route gets 89.6% of all new questions (3 runs) vs the 85 mark; matched-practice talker steps hit 98.8% on new chain questions. Needs more skill families and a sealed check.

roadmap.t: Fair scaling: does a bigger core help?
roadmap.n: Done, result in between: 64.4%, 65.3%, 66.3% for 9.0M, 17.9M, 35.8M, gain +1.9 vs +5 mark (CI -1.0 to +4.8). The core is not the limit. The 35.8M system beats the bare 1.2B 8-shot, 66.3 vs 62.5.
Designed and approved by Ben; not built. Earlier matching-sleep test missed its bar.
Designed; needs a code change before it can run.

roadmap.t: Sealed head-to-head: beat 1-2B models at whole size
roadmap.n: Whole size counts the borrowed 1.2B LM. Only a bare-1.2B comparison on English exists. The 350M LM swap failed (65.7% vs 92.6%); a middle-layer reader is untested.
Core pipeline end to end on the real model.
Paused by Ben on Oct 3 (about 11:07 AM ET). PRs #22, #24, #25, #26, #28.

roadmap.t: Size target: ship a model of about 400M
roadmap.n: Plan: EmbeddingGemma 2 reader (271M, borrowed, frozen) + our own thinker grown to about 100M + talker of about 25M. Nothing borrowed thinks. Growth ladder of 3M, 10M and 30M: each step must gain more from size than the plain model does (30M on hold). The big run is gated by the principles scorecard (Oct 31 readout), not by G1. Size note: the 100M model is 373M as built; the 30M rung is about 301M. Launch waits on group 2 passing at 3M with hand-code count 0.
roadmap.eta: Ladder about 1 week of PC time after it starts; not started
